body.p: Accordingly, Claims 1-16 are currently pending for consideration. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration in view of the remarks set forth below.
A. Claim Interpretation under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f)

The Office Action alleges that the claims invoke 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) because the claims allegedly recite a generic placeholder that is coupled with functional language without reciting sufficient structure to perform the recited function and the generic placeholder is not preceded by a structural modifier.
Applicant does not concede to the Office's assertion that the claims invoke 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) but acquiesces to the claims being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) for examination purposes.
B. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. X101

The following remarks are not to be used for claim construction or any other similar purpose, but are presented solely in connection with the § 101 analysis. Applicant further reserves the rights to make additional arguments.

The Office Action asserts that the Claims 9-12 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 because the claims are allegedly directed to non-statutory subject matter. Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection and disagrees that the claims are directed to an abstract idea, as alleged by the Office.

Further, Claim 9 recites "controlling, with the control device, the vehicle to stop immediately before the intersection", which is not a mental process that can be performed in the human mind. Rather, "controlling, with the control device, the vehicle to stop immediately before the intersection", is an integration of the alleged abstract idea into a practical application, which renders Claim 9 eligible subject matter. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration in view of the above remarks.
C. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. & 102
Claims 1-12 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1)/(2) as being anticipated by U.S. 2021/0061269 to Petroff et al. (hereinafter "Petroff').
1. Rationale of 35 U.S.C. 102

"For a prior art reference to anticipate a claim under 35 U.S.C. § 102, every element of the claimed subject matter must be identically shown in a single reference." Diversitech Corp. v. Century Steps, Inc., 850 F.2d 675, 677, 7 U.S.P.Q. 2d 1315, 1317 (Fed. Cir. 1988) (emphasis added). Further, the elements must be "arranged and combined as required by the claim." Net MoneyIN, Inc. v. VeriSign, Inc., 545 F.3d 1359 (Fed. Cir. 2008).
2. Independent Claim 1
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection of Claim 1 but has amended the claim to expedite allowance. As amended, Claim 1 recites in part:
a control unit controlling the velocity of the vehicle by setting a maximum
velocity, as an upper limit velocity of the vehicle, at which the vehicle can stop immediately before the intersection when the vehicle on the traveling road has no
right of way.

Applicant respectfully asserts that Petroff fails to disclose at least the above feature(s) of amended Claim 1. For example, Petroff does not teach the feature(s) "setting a maximum velocity, as an upper limit velocity of the vehicle, at which the vehicle can stop immediately before the intersection".

In the rejection of Claim 1, the Office asserts that Petroff at [0033] teaches "the vehicle's rules for operation may require the AV 102 stop at the stop line 305 in all instances such as if a stop sign is positioned at the intersection 110; require the AV 102 to stop at the stop line 305 in some instances such as if a traffic signal positioned at the intersection 110 has an active red light".

Therefore, for at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully asserts that Petroff fails to disclose each and every feature of amended Claim 1. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
3. Independent Claims 8-12
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection of Claims 8-12 but has been amended the claims to expedite allowance. Claims 8-12 have been amended similarly as Claim 1.

Therefore, for at least the same reasons as asserted above with respect to amended Claim 1, Applicant respectfully asserts that Petroff fails to disclose each and every feature of amended Claims 8-12. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
4. Dependent Claims 2-7

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejections but submits that each of the dependent Claims 2-7 depends directly or indirectly on independent Claim 1. Thus, dependent Claims 2-7 incorporate by reference all the features of independent Claim 1. In view of the features as recited in the independent Claim 1, and in view of the additional features as recited in the dependent claims, Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 2-7 are allowable for at least the reasons discussed above and their respective additional novel features. Although Applicant has not discussed specific features of all of the dependent claims in this response, Applicant does not necessarily agree with the characterizations and assessments made by the Examiner with respect to the dependent claims. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 2-7 are allowable.
D. New Claims 13-16
New Claims 13-16 have been added. Applicant respectfully requests favorable consideration of the claims.
